LanguageData.CC_SetSec_TradeScreen_Note: The game's trade screen with price sorts, advice from what the colony needs, and what the trade leaves. It only suggests: nothing is traded until you press Accept.
LanguageData.CC_Settings_TradeSorts: Price sorts on the trade screen
LanguageData.CC_Settings_TradeSorts_Tip: Five more sorts in the trade screen's two "Sort by" menus, each the highest first: what the trader pays and what it asks (the trade prices for your negotiator, as the price columns show them, not the market value), the price per kg (for a caravan's load), the best deal (the price against the usual: a sale above it or a purchase under it, with Vanilla Trading Expanded's market counted), and Rimfolk's suggestions first. A good with nothing on that side goes last. With the deeper game hooks they show only on the trade screen; without them they also show in the caravan and transport pod windows, where they sort by market value. Trade Helper's side panel is left as it is.
LanguageData.CC_SetNote_TradeSorts: The trade screen sorts by what the trader pays or asks, by kg, by the best deal, or suggestions first.
LanguageData.CC_Settings_TradeMarks: Marks for what to sell, buy and keep
LanguageData.CC_Settings_TradeMarks_Tip: A small mark beside a good on the trade screen, with why in its tooltip. Worth selling (a mark pointing down): what is beyond what the colony keeps, things no one here can use (clothes no one can wear, a weapon biocoded to someone gone, a techprint learned, a drug taken for pleasure that no drug policy allows), the worse of the spare weapons and clothes when better ones are stored, and a price a fifth above the usual on what is beyond the need. Worth buying (a mark pointing up): food short of the days the plan ahead keeps (the winter ahead counted), medicine, feed, what the blueprints and frames lack, the plan ahead's shopping list, components where machines break down, a colonist's open wish, a techprint or book for the research under way, and a price a fifth under the usual where a stock the colony keeps is low. Kept (a pin): what is set aside for the blueprints, a journey's packing, a promise, a gift for a wish, the drug policies or a contract; it turns red when the trade sells into it. What the colony keeps of a good: what it uses in a season by its record, or a floor for its kind (50 a person of wood, metal and stone blocks, 25 of cloth and leather, 3 of components and of medicine, 5 of gold and the like), and as much again, with what is set aside on top. Only what the colony has and can use counts. Trade Helper's wish list marks what you asked for; these marks are the colony's own, and the two show side by side. Needs the deeper game hooks.
LanguageData.CC_SetNote_TradeMarks: Goods worth selling, worth buying or kept carry a mark on the trade screen, with why.
LanguageData.CC_Settings_TradeBasket_Tip: Two buttons at the foot of the trade screen. Fill suggested puts the marked goods into the trade within the silver both sides have: what the colony is short of first (food, medicine, feed, the plans' materials), then what it has more of than it keeps; rows you set yourself stay as they are and their silver counts first. You see the counts in the game's own columns and confirm with its Accept, or Clear suggested takes them back out. Not in gift mode, or where the trader deals in favor. Needs the deeper game hooks.
LanguageData.CC_SetNote_TradeBasket: A button puts the marked goods into the trade within both sides' silver; another takes them out.
LanguageData.CC_Settings_TradeReadouts: Silver and food after the trade
LanguageData.CC_Settings_TradeReadouts_Tip: Under the silver row, what each side has after the trade, in red when it runs short. At the foot of a trade at home, how many days the colony's food lasts now and after the trade (a caravan's own days of food and its mass after the trade are the game's, at the top). With Vanilla Trading Expanded, the silver the colony keeps in its banks. With Trade Helper loaded the silver after the trade is left out, since its lists of what is bought and sold already say what the trade comes to. Needs the deeper game hooks.
LanguageData.CC_SetNote_TradeReadouts: The trade screen shows each side's silver after the trade, and the colony's days of food.
LanguageData.CC_Settings_TradeMarket_Tip: Point at either price of a good on the trade screen for a card beside the mouse, on the other side from the game's own price tooltip. With Vanilla Trading Expanded it shows the good's market value now against its usual worth and against its average of the last 30 days, its change over the last 7 and 30 days, its lowest and highest of the last 60 days with a drawn line of them, the news that last moved it, and what this trade is likely to do to its price by Vanilla Trading Expanded's own rule for the colony's trades. With the colony's trade record on, the last price the colony got and paid a piece for it, to whom and how long ago, and the best of the last 15 days. A good whose market value moved notably (a tenth in 7 days, or a fifth in 30) gets a small line beside its name, its card on it. A Market button on the silver row opens a window of the trade's goods, sortable, the biggest movers first. Needs the deeper game hooks.
LanguageData.CC_SetNote_TradeMarket: A card on a good's prices with its market and the colony's last prices, and a Market window.
LanguageData.CC_Settings_TradeRecord_Tip: When a trade goes through, what the colony sold and bought, to whom and at what price a piece, is noted: the last 5 trades of each good and 50 goods, the good traded longest ago going first. Silver trades only, never gifts, people or animals. The market card and the Market window show it, with or without Vanilla Trading Expanded. Needs the deeper game hooks.
LanguageData.CC_SetNote_TradeRecord: The colony notes what it sold and bought, to whom and for how much a piece.
LanguageData.CC_Settings_TradeVte: Its market and contracts on the trade screen
LanguageData.CC_Settings_TradeVte_Tip: With Vanilla Trading Expanded, which draws nothing on the trade screen itself: its world market's price of each good against the good's usual worth counts in the best-deal sort and the marks (a good in demand fetches a good price, one in surplus is a bargain) and is named in a mark's tooltip; the goods a contract on its terminal asks of the colony are kept, and worth buying where this trader's price leaves the reward well ahead; the colony's own contracts are worth buying here when the trader asks less than they offer; and the silver in its banks shows at the foot. Read only: nothing of it is changed.
LanguageData.CC_SetNote_TradeVte: With Vanilla Trading Expanded: its prices, contracts and banks count on the trade screen.
LanguageData.CC_Settings_TradeVteHistory: Its price history on the trade screen
LanguageData.CC_Settings_TradeVteHistory_Tip: Vanilla Trading Expanded keeps one price a day of every good its market trades, and moves them with its news, the colony's own trades and a slow drift back toward the usual. With this on, the trade screen reads that history: the market part of the card and of the Market window, the small trend line beside a good whose price moved, a "price change" sort in the Sort by menus (the biggest moves first), what this trade is likely to do to the price (by its own rule: every three days, a chance by the market worth the colony traded of a good, down for a sale and up for a purchase), and reasons more in the marks' tooltips (a sale at the highest of 60 days, a buy at the lowest, a price falling or rising fast). Read only: nothing of it is changed.
LanguageData.CC_SetNote_TradeVteHistory: With Vanilla Trading Expanded: its price history, trends and news on the trade screen.
